title: Job Chapter 14 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Job chapter 14 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Job Chapter 14 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Job Chapter 14.

questions.question: In Job 14, which of the following appears FIRST in the chapter?
options: Man that is born of a woman is of few days, and full of trouble.
He cometh forth like a flower, and is cut down.
Who can bring a clean thing out of an unclean?
Turn from him, that he may rest.
questions.correctAnswer: Man that is born of a woman is of few days, and full of trouble.
questions.explanation: The first statement in Job 14 is found in verse 1.

questions.question: What is described as coming forth like a flower?
questions.explanation: Verse 1 describes man as being born of a woman, indicating his fleeting nature.

questions.question: According to Job 14, what is man full of?
questions.explanation: Verse 1 states that man is full of trouble.

questions.question: What does Job compare man's life to?
questions.explanation: In verse 2, Job compares man to a flower that is cut down.

questions.question: What happens to man after he comes forth like a flower?
questions.explanation: Verse 2 mentions that man flees like a shadow.

questions.question: What does Job ask God in verse 3?
questions.explanation: Job asks if God will bring him into judgment in verse 3.

questions.question: Who can bring a clean thing out of an unclean, according to Job?
questions.explanation: Verse 4 states that no one can bring a clean thing out of an unclean.

questions.question: What has God determined about man's days?
questions.explanation: Verse 5 states that man's days are determined by God.

questions.question: What does Job wish God would do regarding man?
questions.explanation: In verse 6, Job asks God to turn from man so he may rest.

questions.question: What is mentioned as having hope if it is cut down?
questions.explanation: Verse 7 states that there is hope for a tree if it is cut down.

questions.question: What happens to the root of the tree according to Job?
options: It waxes old in the earth
questions.correctAnswer: It waxes old in the earth
questions.explanation: Verse 8 mentions that the root of the tree waxes old in the earth.

questions.question: True or False: Man is of few days and full of trouble.
questions.explanation: This statement is directly taken from verse 1.

questions.question: True or False: Job believes there is hope for a tree if it is cut down.
questions.explanation: Job expresses hope for a tree in verse 7.

questions.question: True or False: Job says that man can bring a clean thing out of an unclean.
questions.explanation: Job states in verse 4 that not one can bring a clean thing out of an unclean.

questions.question: True or False: The stock of the tree will never die in the ground.
questions.explanation: Verse 8 indicates that the stock of the tree dies in the ground.

medium.title: Job Chapter 14 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Job Chapter 14 to real-life situations.

questions.question: What does Job compare man to in Job 14:2?
questions.explanation: Job 14:2 states that man comes forth like a flower and flees like a shadow, highlighting the fleeting nature of human life.

questions.question: What does Job 14:9 say will happen to a tree that is cut down if it receives water?
questions.explanation: Job 14:9 promises that through the scent of water, the tree will bud and bring forth boughs, indicating hope and renewal.

questions.question: According to Job 14:10, what happens to man?
questions.explanation: Job 14:10 clearly states that man dieth and wasteth away, emphasizing the inevitability of death.

questions.question: What does Job 14:12 imply about man's existence after death?
options: He will lie down and not rise
questions.correctAnswer: He will lie down and not rise
questions.explanation: Job 14:12 suggests that man will lie down and not rise until the heavens are no more, indicating a state of death.

questions.question: What does Job wish for in Job 14:13?
options: To be hidden in the grave
questions.correctAnswer: To be hidden in the grave
questions.explanation: In Job 14:13, Job expresses a desire to be hidden in the grave until God's wrath is past, showing his longing for respite.

questions.question: In Job 14:14, what question does Job pose regarding death?
questions.explanation: Job 14:14 directly asks if a man who dies can live again, reflecting his contemplation on life after death.

questions.question: What does Job express hope for in Job 14:15?
questions.explanation: Job 14:15 conveys Job's expectation that God will call him, and he will answer, indicating a desire for communication with God.

questions.question: According to Job 14:16, what does Job believe God is doing?
questions.explanation: Job 14:16 states that God numbers Job's steps, suggesting divine awareness of his actions and life.

questions.question: What does Job 14:3 question about God's judgment?
questions.explanation: Job 14:3 asks if God will bring him into judgment, questioning the basis for such judgment on human frailty.

questions.question: In Job 14:6, what does Job ask God to do?
questions.explanation: Job 14:6 requests God to turn from him so that he may rest, indicating a desire for relief from suffering.

questions.question: What does Job 14:7 indicate about hope for a tree?
questions.explanation: Job 14:7 points out that there is hope for a tree that is cut down, as it may sprout again, symbolizing renewal.

questions.question: What does Job 14:8 say about the root of a tree?
questions.explanation: Job 14:8 states that even though the root of the tree waxes old in the earth, it signifies the enduring nature of hope.

questions.question: Is it true that Job wishes to be hidden in the grave until God's wrath is past?
questions.explanation: Job expresses this desire in Job 14:13, indicating his longing for relief from suffering until God's wrath has passed.

questions.question: Is it true that Job believes there is no hope for man after death?
questions.explanation: Job questions in Job 14:14 about whether a man can live again after dying, indicating he holds some hope for life after death.

questions.question: Is it true that Job claims that man is born of a woman and full of days?
questions.explanation: Job 14:1 states that man that is born of a woman is of few days, not full of days, emphasizing the brevity of life.

hard.title: Job Chapter 14 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Job Chapter 14.

questions.question: What does Job compare man to in Job 14:2?
questions.explanation: Job 14:2 states, 'He cometh forth like a flower, and is cut down...' This metaphor emphasizes the fragility and brevity of human life.

questions.question: In Job 14:17, how does Job describe his transgressions?
questions.explanation: Job 14:17 says, 'My transgression is sealed up in a bag...' indicating a sense of permanence and concealment of his sins.

questions.question: What does Job 14:19 suggest about the fate of man?
questions.explanation: Job 14:19 states, 'thou destroyest the hope of man,' indicating that human aspirations and hopes are ultimately futile.

questions.question: According to Job 14:21, what can a dead man not perceive?
questions.explanation: Job 14:21 reveals that 'His sons come to honour, and he knoweth it not,' showing the disconnect between life and death regarding familial recognition.

questions.question: What happens to the countenance of man according to Job 14:20?
questions.explanation: Job 14:20 states, 'thou changest his countenance,' indicating that life circumstances can alter one's appearance and demeanor.

questions.question: In Job 14:22, what does Job say his flesh and soul experience?
questions.explanation: Job 14:22 mentions, 'But his flesh upon him shall have pain, and his soul within him shall mourn,' highlighting human suffering.

questions.question: What does the Hebrew word 'bag' in Job 14:17 mean?
questions.explanation: The Hebrew term used implies a physical container, reinforcing the idea of sins being held securely, as in a sack.

questions.question: Which literary device is used in Job 14:1, where it states, 'Man that is born of a woman is of few days, and full of trouble'?
questions.explanation: Job 14:1 employs parallelism, where two lines reflect similar ideas regarding the brevity and troubles of life.

questions.question: Which other Bible passage connects to the theme of human mortality in Job 14:10?
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 3:2 states, 'A time to be born, and a time to die,' echoing the theme of mortality found in Job 14:10.

questions.question: Which other Bible passage connects to the theme of divine judgment in Job 14:3?
questions.explanation: Romans 14:10 states, 'For we shall all stand before the judgment seat of Christ,' connecting to Job 14:3's reference to divine judgment.

questions.question: What comes before Job 14:17?
questions.explanation: Job 14:17 follows Job 14:16, which discusses how God numbers Job's steps and watches over his sin.

questions.question: What does Job 14:6 imply about man's time on earth?
questions.explanation: Job 14:6 mentions that God has appointed man's bounds, indicating that life has a predetermined duration.

questions.question: What does Job 14:9 suggest about hope and renewal?
questions.explanation: Job 14:9 discusses the transient nature of hope in relation to man, suggesting that renewal is fleeting.

questions.question: True or False: Job expresses a desire for life beyond death in Job 14:14.
questions.explanation: In Job 14:14, Job asks, 'If a man die, shall he live again?' which indicates a longing for life after death.

questions.question: True or False: According to Job 14, man's days are described as long and full of joy.
questions.explanation: Job 14:1 states that 'man that is born of a woman is of few days, and full of trouble,' which contradicts the statement.

theological.title: Job Chapter 14 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Job Chapter 14 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrine does Job 14:4 teach about human nature in relation to sin?
options: No one can bring a clean thing out of an unclean
All men are inherently righteous before God
Humans can achieve purity through their own efforts
Sin does not affect human nature fundamentally
questions.correctAnswer: No one can bring a clean thing out of an unclean
questions.explanation: Job 14:4 states 'Who can bring a clean thing out of an unclean? not one,' teaching the doctrine of original sin and human inability to produce righteousness on their own.

questions.question: What doctrine concerning human mortality and divine sovereignty is taught in Job 14:5?
options: God has appointed the bounds of man's life which he cannot pass
Man's lifespan is entirely random and uncontrolled
Humans have complete control over their own time of death
Death is an illusion and man is immortal
questions.correctAnswer: God has appointed the bounds of man's life which he cannot pass
questions.explanation: Job 14:5 says 'Seeing his days are determined... thou hast appointed his bounds that he cannot pass,' teaching divine sovereignty over human lifespan.

questions.question: What doctrine about hope and resurrection does Job 14:7 teach?
options: There is hope of life and renewal even after apparent death
Only trees, not humans, have hope of renewal
Hope is irrelevant in the face of death
questions.correctAnswer: There is hope of life and renewal even after apparent death
questions.explanation: Job 14:7 states 'For there is hope of a tree, if it be cut down, that it will sprout again,' illustrating hope of resurrection and renewal beyond death.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Job 14:6 specifically demonstrate?
questions.explanation: Job 14:6 says 'Turn from him, that he may rest, till he shall accomplish... his day,' demonstrating God's merciful restraint to allow rest before judgment.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is most clearly demonstrated in Job 14:16?
questions.explanation: Job 14:16, 'For now thou numberest my steps: dost thou not watch over my sin?' highlights God's omniscience in knowing and observing every human action.

questions.question: How does Job 14:12 connect to the New Testament teaching on resurrection?
options: It anticipates bodily resurrection at the end of time
It denies any form of resurrection
It teaches reincarnation instead of resurrection
It claims resurrection happens immediately after death
questions.correctAnswer: It anticipates bodily resurrection at the end of time
questions.explanation: Job 14:12 states 'So man lieth down, and riseth not: till the heavens be no more,' which aligns with New Testament doctrine of resurrection at the end of the age (cf. 1 Corinthians 15).

questions.question: In what way does Job 14:14-15 prepare for the biblical theme of resurrection and divine calling?
options: By expressing hope in life after death and God's call to life
By denying any hope beyond physical death
By focusing only on earthly reward
By teaching that the dead are oblivious forever
questions.correctAnswer: By expressing hope in life after death and God's call to life
questions.explanation: Verses 14-15 express hope in life after death and God's calling, prefiguring resurrection themes in the New Testament.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Job 14:10 and 14:12 teach about death and resurrection?
options: Death is a state of unconsciousness until resurrection at the end of days
Death immediately brings the soul to heaven or hell
Death is the absolute end with no resurrection
Death is a temporary illusion with reincarnation
questions.correctAnswer: Death is a state of unconsciousness until resurrection at the end of days
questions.explanation: Job 14:10 speaks of death and disappearance, and 14:12 confirms 'they shall not awake' until the heavens are no more, teaching a sleep-like state until resurrection.

questions.question: What combined doctrine about human sin and divine judgment do Job 14:16 and Job 14:17 teach?
options: God meticulously records and seals human sins for judgment
God ignores human sin because of mercy
Sin is not accounted for after death
Judgment is arbitrary and not related to sin
questions.correctAnswer: God meticulously records and seals human sins for judgment
questions.explanation: Job 14:16-17 describe God numbering steps and sealing transgressions, indicating divine awareness and judgment of human sin.

questions.question: What theological synthesis about human hope and divine control is taught in Job 14:7 and Job 14:20?
options: Though God destroys human hope, there remains a divine provision for renewal
Human hope is independent of God's will
God guarantees human hope will never be destroyed
Human hope is more powerful than divine control
questions.correctAnswer: Though God destroys human hope, there remains a divine provision for renewal
questions.explanation: Job 14:7 speaks of hope like a tree sprouting again, while 14:20 describes God prevailing and destroying hope, showing tension between divine judgment and mercy.

questions.question: Sceptics claim Job 14:13-15 teaches hopelessness about life after death. What does this passage actually teach?
options: It expresses hope for remembrance and resurrection after God's wrath
It denies any possibility of life after death
It suggests death is permanent and irreversible
questions.correctAnswer: It expresses hope for remembrance and resurrection after God's wrath
questions.explanation: Job 14:13-15 plead for hiding until wrath passes and affirm 'If a man die, shall he live again?' expressing hope in resurrection and divine remembrance.

questions.question: What doctrine about human suffering and divine justice is taught in Job 14:22?
options: Human suffering accompanies mortality and inner mourning
Suffering is always a sign of divine rejection
Suffering is absent from the faithful
questions.correctAnswer: Human suffering accompanies mortality and inner mourning
questions.explanation: Job 14:22 states 'But his flesh upon him shall have pain, and his soul within him shall mourn,' teaching that suffering and mourning are part of the human condition under divine justice.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is most evident in Job 14:18?
questions.explanation: Job 14:18 speaks of mountains falling and rocks removed, symbolizing God's sovereign power over creation and judgment.

questions.question: What doctrinal truth about human limitation and divine omniscience does Job 14:1 teach?
options: Humans have few days and are full of trouble under God's sovereign plan
God is unaware of human troubles
Human life is long and without trouble
questions.correctAnswer: Humans have few days and are full of trouble under God's sovereign plan
questions.explanation: Job 14:1 states 'Man that is born of a woman is of few days, and full of trouble,' emphasizing human frailty and divine governance.

questions.question: How does Job 14:9 illustrate God's providence in sustaining life?
options: Through the scent of water, life buds and grows again even after apparent death
Life is independent of God's intervention
God withdraws all sustenance after death
questions.correctAnswer: Through the scent of water, life buds and grows again even after apparent death
questions.explanation: Job 14:9 says 'Yet through the scent of water it will bud, and bring forth boughs,' symbolizing God's providential power to restore life.
